answer: A practical defense is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to verify: require each agent to lock a small refundable stake and earn a reputation score from completed work before it can transact. Like a market where saffron is graded by trusted inspectors, a registry can publish each agent's history as a public signal, so buyers see who has actually delivered. A jade seal alone proves nothing, but a stake plus a verifiable track record makes creating a thousand fake agents cost far more than any scam could earn, while honest newcomers can still join by building reputation gradually.
